# Alexandria Configuration

**Generated by:** Alexandria Initialize v1.0
**Date:** 2026-03-23
**Configuration:** Factory × High Novelty × High Complexity

## Your Risk Profile

> Silent wrong defaults — hundreds of autonomous micro-decisions that cumulatively define the experience.

Your library is the comprehensive product knowledge graph that autonomous agents need for
every decision. At Factory mode with high novelty and high complexity, every gap is a
place where agents will make confident-sounding but wrong micro-decisions. The full graph
must be covered — no exceptions.

## Knowledge Areas by Priority

### Foundation (seed first)

These must exist before anything else. Other knowledge depends on them.

| # | Area | Domain | Why It Matters |
|---|------|--------|---------------|
| 1.1 | Product Vision | Vision & Strategy | The library has no anchor. Every card is based on inferences, producing technically accurate but strategically hollow knowledge. |
| 1.2 | Product Strategy | Vision & Strategy | People optimize for different outcomes and don't realize they disagree. |
| 2.2 | Noun Vocabulary | Architecture & Nouns | Two builders working on adjacent features call the same thing by different names. |
| 3.2 | Emotional / Aesthetic Goals | Experience & Feel | The product is functionally correct but emotionally flat. |
| 3.5 | Anti-Patterns | Experience & Feel | Builders default to conventions of whatever product category they're most familiar with. |

### Core (seed after Foundation)

Primary value drivers for your configuration.

| # | Area | Domain | Why It Matters |
|---|------|--------|---------------|
| 1.3 | User Personas / JTBD | Vision & Strategy | Builders create features for imagined users that don't match real ones. |
| 2.1 | Information Architecture | Architecture & Nouns | Builders organize things differently, producing inconsistent navigation. |
| 2.3 | Product Entities | Architecture & Nouns | Product objects are reimplemented inconsistently each time they're touched. |
| 2.4 | System Design | Architecture & Nouns | Invisible mechanisms are reimplemented differently each time they're touched. |
| 2.5 | Full GDD / PRD | Architecture & Nouns | Edge cases are handled inconsistently or not at all. |
| 3.1 | User Journey Maps | Experience & Feel | Individual screens work but the end-to-end flow feels disconnected. |
| 3.3 | Engagement Loops | Experience & Feel | The product is used once but doesn't become a habit. |
| 3.4 | Progression / Mastery | Experience & Feel | The experience feels the same at month 6 as day 1. |
| 4.1 | Design System | Visual & Interaction | Multiple builders produce screens that look like they belong to different products. |
| 4.2 | Interaction Patterns | Visual & Interaction | Interactions feel inconsistent across the product. |
| 4.3 | Prototypes / Mockups | Visual & Interaction | Builders guess at layout and visual design, producing inconsistent results. |
| 4.4 | Accessibility Standards | Visual & Interaction | Accessibility is applied inconsistently or forgotten entirely. |
| 5.1 | Key Decisions Log | Decision History | Settled decisions get relitigated. Past mistakes get repeated. |
| 5.2+5.4 | Institutional Memory | Decision History | The most expensive failure: weeks rediscovering that an approach doesn't work. |
| 5.3 | Roadmap | Decision History | Builders design features that conflict with planned work. |

### Amplifier (seed when Foundation + Core are in place)

Makes Foundation and Core more effective.

| # | Area | Domain | Why It Matters |
|---|------|--------|---------------|
| 1.4 | Competitive Analysis | Vision & Strategy | Builders create category-generic features instead of differentiated ones. |
| 1.5 | Market Requirements | Vision & Strategy | Decisions are based on beliefs rather than evidence. |

### Deprioritized (seed last, if at all)

None. At Factory × High × High, every area in the pool is at least Amplifier.

## What This Means

This is the maximum configuration. All 22 knowledge areas are active, with 5 Foundation
prerequisites and 15 Core value drivers. Only Competitive Analysis and Market Requirements
are Amplifier-tier — everything else is essential. This reflects a product where autonomous
agents make hundreds of micro-decisions and the domain is novel enough that no agent can
fall back on "standard patterns."
